blocks.markdown:
**Pollution** is when harmful things get into the air, water or land.

Plastic can take hundreds of years to break down.
blocks.say: Pollution is when harmful things get into the air, water or land and make them dirty or unsafe. Smoke from factories and cars pollutes the air. Chemicals and rubbish in rivers pollute the water. And plastic bags and bottles left on the ground pollute the land. Pollution harms people, animals and plants. Plastic is a big problem, because it can take hundreds of years to break down.

blocks.markdown:
The three Rs are **reduce**, **reuse** and **recycle**.

Recycling turns used materials into new things.
blocks.say: We can fight pollution with three Rs: reduce, reuse and recycle. Reduce means to use less, for example by carrying a cloth bag. Reuse means to use things again, like refilling a bottle. Recycle means turning used things into new ones, like paper, glass, metal and some plastics. At a recycling centre, materials are sorted, cleaned and made into new things. Using buses, bikes or walking also reduces air pollution.

blocks.title: Fatima's planet-friendly day
blocks.transcript: Fatima's family has solar panels on the roof of their home. Sunlight is renewable energy. It will not run out. She turns off the tap while she brushes her teeth. At school, they reduce, reuse and then recycle. She chooses local fruit with fewer food miles. Cargo ships carry goods between countries. Fair trade helps farmers get a fair price. Small choices by many people help our one planet.
blocks.caption: Fatima follows her family's energy, waste and trade choices for a day and learns what sustainable means.

blocks.markdown:
About 97 percent of Earth's water is salty. Only a little is **fresh water** we can use.

We can save water by fixing leaks and not leaving taps running.
blocks.say: Water is precious. About ninety-seven percent of the water on Earth is salty. Most of the rest is frozen in ice. Only a very small amount is fresh water that we can use. That is why we must not waste it. Turn off the tap while brushing teeth. Fix dripping taps and take short showers. Water plants with leftover water. In Pakistan, the Indus gives much of our fresh water, so saving it helps farmers and cities.

blocks.markdown:
Coal, oil and gas are **fossil fuels**. They will run out and cause pollution.

**Renewable** energy comes from the Sun, wind and water, and does not run out.
blocks.say: We use energy for light, cooking, and moving machines. Coal, oil and gas are fossil fuels. They took millions of years to form and will run out, and they cause pollution when burned. Renewable energy comes from sources that do not run out, like the Sun, wind and flowing water. Pakistan has dams like Tarbela on the Indus that make electricity from water. Many homes now use solar panels.

blocks.markdown:
A **need** is something we must have. A **want** is something nice to have.

People earn money, and can spend it or save it.
blocks.say: Money helps us get the things we need. A need is something we must have to live well, such as food, water, clothes and a home. A want is something nice to have but not essential, such as a new toy. People earn money by working, and they can spend it or save it. Saving means keeping some for later, so we have enough for something important. Wise people think before they spend.

blocks.alt: Bread and a home are needs. A toy and a game are wants.

blocks.markdown:
**Exports** are sold to other countries. **Imports** are bought from other countries.

Pakistan exports rice, cloth and footballs. It imports oil and machines.
blocks.say: No country has everything it needs. So countries trade. Goods that a country sells to other countries are called exports. Goods that a country buys from other countries are called imports. Pakistan exports rice, cotton cloth, leather goods and sports goods, such as the footballs made in Sialkot. It imports things like oil and machines. Trade helps everyone get more of what they need.

blocks.markdown:
The **Silk Road** was a network of trade routes between China and the Mediterranean.

Traders travelled in **caravans** of camels.
blocks.say: About two thousand years ago, traders began to carry goods from China to the Mediterranean Sea. This network of routes was named the Silk Road, because silk was one of the most precious goods. The routes crossed deserts, mountains and rivers. Traders travelled in caravans of camels, because camels can carry heavy loads over long distances in the desert. Some routes passed through what is now northern Pakistan, and cities like Taxila were busy trading places.

scenes.caption: China: silk is packed.
scenes.say: The journey begins in China, where silk is made and packed.

scenes.caption: The caravan crosses the mountains.
scenes.say: The caravan crosses deserts and high mountains, including the Karakoram in the north of Pakistan.

scenes.caption: Taxila and trading cities.
scenes.say: In cities such as Taxila, traders swapped goods, and ideas as well as goods were exchanged.

scenes.caption: The goods reach the Mediterranean.
scenes.say: At the far end, in the Mediterranean, silk and spices reached the markets of Europe.

question.explanation: A caravan is a group of traders and animals travelling together.

options.text: A group of travellers and animals together

blocks.markdown:
Silk, spices, glass and paper travelled the Silk Road.

**Ideas** and inventions travelled too.
blocks.say: Traders did not only carry silk. They also carried spices like pepper, glass, paper, tea, horses and precious stones. But something even more important travelled too: ideas. Inventions such as paper and new ideas in maths, medicine and religion spread along the roads. The Silk Road shows us that when people trade and meet, they share knowledge. Everyone learns from each other.

blocks.prompt: Why were the Silk Road routes so important to the world?
